articles.title: Austin Software Company Cuts 120 Jobs as Other Area Employers Keep Hiring
articles.text:
AUSTIN — A local software company announced on June 1, 2026, that it will lay off 120 employees, marking one of the larger workforce reductions in the city's technology sector this year.

The company said in a statement that the cuts affect staff across several departments and are part of an effort to reduce costs and refocus on its core products. Affected employees were notified Monday, according to the statement, and will receive severance pay along with job placement assistance. The company did not say whether further reductions are planned.

The announcement adds to a period of uncertainty for some workers in Austin's technology industry, where several firms have trimmed staff over the past year. Local workforce officials said they plan to share information about job resources with those affected.

Not all of the region's major employers are pulling back, however. Several of the area's large organizations, including Austin System A, continue to post openings and recruit new staff, offering potential opportunities for job seekers in the local market.

A spokesperson for the software company said leadership regretted the decision and thanked departing employees for their contributions. The company said it expects the reductions to be completed by the end of the month.

articles.title: Austin System B Opens Expanded Cardiac Catheterization Lab, Seeks Nurses and Technologists
articles.text:
AUSTIN — Austin System B opened an expanded cardiac catheterization lab on Oct. 1, 2024, adding capacity for heart procedures as demand for cardiovascular care continues to grow in the region.

The expanded lab adds procedure rooms and updated imaging equipment used to diagnose and treat blocked arteries, irregular heart rhythms and other cardiac conditions. A system spokesperson said the expansion is intended to shorten wait times for scheduled procedures and improve the system's ability to respond quickly to patients arriving with heart attacks.

To staff the larger unit, Austin System B is hiring registered nurses and cardiovascular technologists. The spokesperson said the positions include full-time and part-time roles, and that the system is welcoming applications from both experienced cardiac professionals and clinicians interested in training for the specialty.

The system's chief executive described the opening as part of a continuing effort to bring advanced cardiac services closer to home for Austin-area residents. "Heart care is one of the most time-sensitive services we provide," the chief executive said in a statement. "This expansion gives our teams more room and better tools to care for patients when every minute counts."

The system's chief nursing officer said the new positions offer a chance for nurses and technologists to join a growing cardiac program. Information about open roles is available through the system's careers page, the spokesperson said.

articles.title: Austin System C Opens Expanded Cardiac Catheterization Lab, Begins Hiring Push

The expansion adds procedure rooms and updated imaging equipment designed to shorten wait times for diagnostic heart catheterizations, stent placements and related treatments. A system spokesperson said the larger lab will allow care teams to schedule more patients each day and respond more quickly to emergency cardiac cases.

"Heart disease remains one of the leading health concerns in our community, and this expansion helps us meet that need closer to home," the system's chief executive said in a statement. "We're proud to invest in our cardiac program and in the people who make it work."

To support the expanded lab, Austin System C is hiring registered nurses with cardiac or critical care experience, as well as cardiovascular and radiologic technologists. The spokesperson said the positions include day and on-call shifts, and that the system is welcoming both experienced professionals and recent graduates interested in cardiac care. The lab's medical director said the new layout was planned with input from physicians, nurses and technologists who work in the unit. "Our team helped shape this space, and that shows in how efficiently it runs," the medical director said.

articles.title: Charlotte System A Announces Merger With Out-of-Area Regional Health System
articles.text:
CHARLOTTE — Charlotte System A announced this week that it has agreed to merge with a regional health system based outside the Charlotte metro area, a move that would expand the local provider's reach across a wider portion of the region.

The announcement, made on May 5, 2025, did not identify the partner by name in initial public statements. A spokesperson for Charlotte System A described the partner as a regional health system with hospitals and outpatient sites serving communities beyond the metro.

The system's chief executive said in a statement that the combination is intended to strengthen patient access, share clinical expertise and improve the organizations' ability to invest in services over the long term. "Bringing our organizations together positions us to better serve patients across a larger footprint," the chief executive said.

Details on the deal's financial terms, leadership structure and timeline for completion were not disclosed. A hospital spokesperson said further information would be shared with employees, patients and the community as the process moves forward, and that day-to-day operations at Charlotte System A facilities are not expected to change in the near term.

Mergers between health systems typically require review and approvals before they can be finalized. Charlotte System A did not say when it expects the transaction to close.

articles.title: Two Months After Merger Announcement, Charlotte System A Staff Face Lingering Uncertainty
articles.text:
CHARLOTTE, July 5, 2025 — Roughly two months after Charlotte System A announced its planned merger, employees across the health system say questions about their futures remain largely unanswered, with cardiologists among the most concerned.

Several physicians in the system's cardiology group said this week that they have not received clear guidance on whether their current employment contracts will be honored, renegotiated or replaced once the combination is finalized. One cardiologist, speaking on condition of anonymity because staff were not authorized to discuss the matter publicly, said colleagues are weighing their options while they wait for details on compensation, call schedules and noncompete terms.

A spokesperson for Charlotte System A said the system values its physicians and is committed to communicating with staff as the merger process moves forward. The spokesperson said contract-related decisions are still under review and that leadership expects to share more information in the coming months.

Nurses and support staff have also raised questions about benefits and reporting structures, according to employees who attended recent internal meetings. Some said leadership has held listening sessions, but that answers on specifics have been limited so far.

Health care observers note that periods of uncertainty after merger announcements are common, and that retaining specialists such as cardiologists can be a key concern for systems going through consolidation. For now, many Charlotte System A employees say they are continuing to care for patients while waiting to learn how the merger will reshape their jobs.
